newsitem.title: USA: AT&T to up some residential, business rates.
newsitem.headline: AT&T to up some residential, business rates.

text.p: AT&T Corp said on Wednesday it would increase certain of its long distance rates for residential and small business customers.

The company said basic rates for domestic, direct-dialed, state-to-state calls made from a consumer's home would rise 5.9 percent. The residential price increases, effective December 1, would have an average impact of about $0.60 per month on a typical consumer's bill, it said.
AT&T also said it would increase rates charged small business customers for international direct-dialed, toll-free and PRO WATS/Plan Q services by 4.8 percent.
It was raising rates to recover significant investments made to broaden its service line, build technical infrastructure and improve customer service, AT&T said.
The company said it would also raise the average rate of calls made with a calling card by five percent and those made with the assistance of an AT&T operator by 2.6 percent.

It would also increase the monthly fees on its Reach Out America, SelectSaver and AnyHour Saver calling plans, it said. AT&T said it stopped actively marketing these plans in 1993, when it introduced its "True" family of calling plans.
